headline: Symmetry constraints shape generative and predictive models of molecular structure
label: Symmetry Aware Molecular Modeling
summary: Recent preprints and papers apply group symmetry and physically defined quantities such as the committor to molecular generative and predictive models.
synthesis: The dominant thread is the incorporation of geometric symmetry and physically defined quantities into molecular learning. A canonicalization approach enforces S_n x SE(3) symmetry in diffusion and flow generative models, with theory and molecular graph generation as applications. MolgraphX applies symmetry sensitivity at the explanation stage, identifying important substructures in graph convolutional property predictors. A graph neural network with geometric vector perceptrons predicts the committor directly from atomic coordinates, giving atom-level interpretability. The quantum-annealing generative paper follows a different route: its Neural Hash Function reportedly improves validity and drug-likeness beyond training data, and its summary cites no explicit symmetry or physics constraint. What is new is treating symmetry as a canonicalization or architectural constraint on generation and interpretation, and linking learned predictors to physically defined quantities. Performance claims in the preprints remain unverified.
